lines.text: The sky should be violet. So why isn't it?
Sunlight scatters in our atmosphere, and short wavelengths scatter the most.
Violet scatters even more than blue.
But the sun gives off less violet, some of it is absorbed high up, and our eyes are weaker at seeing it.
Blue wins that combination. So the sky looks blue.
The sky isn't violet... because of what your eyes can't do.
